source_snapshot.test_set: AMD CPU RAS -PCIe LCRC TX/RX Error
source_snapshot.procedure: Calls for an ECC RDIMM and NIC, uses listpcieslotinfo, then hardcodes socket/die/NBIO 0:0:1, core 3, port 0 with errortype 0 for TX and 1 for RX under AER/severity/SyncFlood settings.
source_snapshot.criteria: Tool PASS and OS correctable-error report within undefined timeout according to unspecified AMD RAS spec.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic AER/ECRC/LCRC/poison/fatal grep blurs distinct error classes and does not prove direction or replay recovery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED; adds NIC mapping and no-production-traffic gate but accepts TX/RX flag meaning, fixed tuple and OS-report expectation without exact counter/evidence authority.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC Plug a NIC (Network Interface Card) device on a target PCIe slot on the SUT / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. NBIO Common options → ACS Enable: Enable b. NBIO Common options → Enable AER Cap: Enable c. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Root Port UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030 d. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Device UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030 e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable f. NBIO Common Options → NBIO RAS Common Options → SyncFlood on PCIe Fatal Error: True 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Execute the following command to get a list of devices in the PCIe slots: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listpcieslotinfo 6. PCIe LCRC TX Error, enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --pcieerror --sockdienbio 0:0:1 --errortype 0 --pciecore 3 --pcieport 0 7. PCIe LCRC RX Error, enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --pcieerror --sockdienbio 0:0:1 --errortype 1 --pciecore 3 --pcieport 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- PCIe slot 1~N: inject the PCIe LCRC on PCIe slot 1~N via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'pcier|aer|ecrc|lcrc|poisoned|fatal'; echo __PCIe_LCRC_on_PCIe_slot_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

disposition_reason: An LCRC fault is detected by the receiving link partner and normally drives replay, so the injection-side label alone does not prove where evidence should appear. TX and RX coverage requires traffic in the corresponding direction plus counters tied to the mapped port. An OS may not emit a generic AER message for every corrected link replay, making link/NIC counters and packet integrity more reliable than a broad log grep. test_case.test_name: PCIe slot 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify correctable LCRC fault handling in both transmit and receive directions for every required PCIe slot, proving the intended link/counter response, bounded packet impact and stable NIC/link operation after each stimulus.
required_package: Physical slot/NIC serial/FW/driver/BDF to socket/die/NBIO/core/port map for every target
AMD tool/spec proof that errortype 0 and 1 represent LCRC TX and RX and identify the observing side
Isolated bidirectional traffic endpoints, packet/checksum/loss oracle and management dependencies
Exact PCIe/NIC/AER status and directional counter expected before/after each injection
Decoded 7EF6030 relevance plus masks, DPC and SyncFlood policy for a correctable LCRC case
Supported OS, timeout, acceptable replay/retrain delta, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration
test_case.test_command: Map each physical NIC/slot to socket, die, NBIO, core and port; prove errortype 0/1 direction semantics; identify local transmitter/receiver and run isolated bidirectional traffic; capture link speed/width, AER and PCIe/NIC error counters; inject TX once and RX once separately; correlate the expected directional counter/status delta without fatal escalation; verify traffic integrity and no retrain/degradation; restore BIOS/HDT/AER state.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.

Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.`; it becomes enforceable only after resolving: Resolve Reliability row 61 Wistron-System RAS-00781-V002: provide PCIe slot/NIC-to-socket/die/NBIO/core/port coverage and vendor proof errortype 0/1 mean LCRC TX/RX with observing-side semantics; justify ECC RDIMM; define isolated bidirectional traffic, direction-specific link/AER/NIC counters and packet/replay/retrain thresholds; approve 7EF6030/masks/DPC/SyncFlood relevance, supported OS, timeout, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.
safety_gate: Dedicated NIC/link with OOB management independent of tested traffic and no production workload
Power/ESD-safe NIC handling and live tuple verification; never reuse 0:0:1/core3/port0 blindly
Run controlled traffic to prove direction and baseline all counters before a single injection
Abort on wrong port/counter, link loss, speed/width downgrade, excessive packet loss, driver reset or fatal/DPC/SyncFlood escalation
No automatic retry; preserve evidence and restore/diff BIOS/HDT/AER/SyncFlood and NIC state
expected_evidence: Tool/spec direction mapping plus decoded AER/severity policy and baseline counters
Isolated traffic endpoint, direction, packet/checksum baseline
Separate TX and RX transcripts with attributable counter/status deltas
Packet outcome, no fatal escalation and restored speed/width/link/driver health
test_case.recovery: If hardware exposes no attributable directional LCRC counter, use an owner-approved link analyzer or tool transcript oracle; do not replace missing direction evidence with generic AER text. ECC RDIMM relevance must be justified or treated as copied source text.

source_conflict.reason: Slot 1~N is reduced to one fixed NBIO/core/port tuple; errortype 0/1 direction semantics are not cited; ECC RDIMM is unexplained; generic logs mix unrelated ECRC/poison/fatal classes; no directed traffic or counter oracle exists. Correctable Criteria coexist with undecoded uncorrectable severity/SyncFlood settings, timeout is undefined and RHEL 2022 ambiguous.
